measurement_scope: Read-only analysis; no measured process, test, compiler, or profiler is executed.
Guest instructions are not CPU cycles or CPU-time percentages. Separate audited elapsed medians are explicitly labeled.
Profiles include startup, input decoding, repeated checksum calls, checksum accumulation, I/O, and exit.
DHAT bytes are requested allocations, not RSS or allocator usable size. Global peaks use simultaneous gb/gbk.
Only checksum is profiled here; these attributions do not establish the costs of verify, generate, or append.

provenance.historical_guard_policy: Original source guards remain in immutable snapshots and the passed historical audit. Current source is intentionally changed; historical executables, manifests, snapshots, raw profiles, complete outputs, and shared immutable source/tool identities are reverified.

rust_control.note: Same executable/input/repetitions; small process-level differences include changed argument paths.

separate_audited_wall_time.note: Elapsed-time batches and repetitions differ from instrumented profiles; no instruction-to-time conversion.

findings: The final checksum loop is scalar: four cursor/load, eight digit arithmetic, and three accumulator/latch instructions per selected digit. No checked arbitrary-integer fallback executes for the profiled ASCII digits.
Digit conversion and tagged storage, reverse-stride subtotal, and immediate-value release scans execute vector instructions. SIMD in these runtime helpers does not imply a vector checksum loop.

The requested allocations inside repeated checksum calls consist of one digit buffer, one list header, and two TLS registrations per process. There are no recurring one-character strings, divmod pairs, slice lists, or comprehension-result buffers.

Remaining work includes materializing tagged digit storage, rescanning it for a subtotal and small-value destruction, scalar digit arithmetic, and fixed helper/cache/normalization calls. Streaming and proof propagation are possible generic future directions, not measured outcomes.

The unchanged Python library and independent Rust reference implement the same outputs with different storage and iteration strategies. Rust streams digits; the compiler still materializes a reusable integer list.

runtime_reuse_contract.ownership: Only empty buffers and uniquely owned empty headers are retained; headers have no buffer. Strong aliases and Weak observers prevent header reuse; no element owners survive caching. TLS teardown and reentrant cache borrowing fall back to normal allocation/destruction.
runtime_reuse_contract.limit: The bound excludes TLS bookkeeping, allocator metadata, and ordinary live program objects.

excluded_exploratory_evidence.reason: R7's runtime was byte-identical to an uncommitted inlining experiment despite a different declared source. None of its timings or profiles enter this final attribution.
The normalization-inlining experiment was not integrated. Its instruction reduction is not evidence of an elapsed-time improvement and is excluded from final comparisons.
